title: Cokernels of maps between finite-presentation modules are finite presentation
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $f:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ be $\mathcal O_X$-linear. If $\mathcal G$ is of finite type (locally a quotient of $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}$ with $m$ finite) and $\mathcal H$ is of finite presentation (locally the cokernel of $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ with $r,n$ finite) [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], then the cokernel of $f$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is of finite presentation. In particular this holds when both $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal H$ are of finite presentation.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0H96 (lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation), lines 1431-1450; used in Properties, Lemma 01PJ, lines 3112-3116

proof.text: Preliminaries on restriction to opens. For an open $U\subseteq X$, $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ is abelian with sectionwise kernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\mathcal M\mapsto\mathcal M|_U$, $\psi\mapsto\psi|_U$ ($(\psi|_U)_W=\psi_W$) is a functor with $(\mathcal M|_U)|_V=\mathcal M|_V$ for $V\subseteq U$. (a) Restriction preserves epimorphisms and exactness of complexes: by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1) and (2) both are local lifting conditions over all opens $W$ and open coverings of them, and for $\mathcal M|_U$ these are the same conditions over the opens $W\subseteq U$. (b) If $c:\mathcal H\to\mathcal C$ is a cokernel of $f:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$, then $c|_U$ is a cokernel of $f|_U$: the complex $\mathcal G\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal H\xrightarrow{c}\mathcal C$ is exact at $\mathcal H$, the image of $f$ being by definition the kernel of its cokernel [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], and $c$ is an epimorphism; by (a) $\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal H|_U\to\mathcal C|_U$ is exact at $\mathcal H|_U$ with $c|_U$ an epimorphism, so $c|_U$ is a cokernel of $f|_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (a). (c) By [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] both 'of finite type' and 'of finite presentation' are conditions on open neighbourhoods of the points, so $\mathcal M$ has the property if every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ with $\mathcal M|_U$ having it as an $\mathcal O_U$-module, and conversely $\mathcal M|_U$ has it if $\mathcal M$ has it (since $(\mathcal M|_U)|_V=\mathcal M|_V$). Both properties pass to isomorphic modules (compose the local epimorphism, resp. the local isomorphism with a cokernel, with the isomorphism restricted to $U$). (d) $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}$ is of finite type (the identity map, sections $e_1,\dots,e_m$). (e) A module of finite presentation is of finite type: if $\theta:\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F|_U$ with $\alpha:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ and cokernel map $c_\alpha$, then $\theta\circ c_\alpha:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$ is an epimorphism (a cokernel map followed by an isomorphism), and it is the map of the $n$ sections $\theta c_\alpha(e_i)$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0H96 (lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation), proof, lines 1440-1454 ('Locally on X'); Definitions 01B5 (line 810) and 01BN (line 1378)

proof.text: Reduction to a presentation of $\mathcal H$ on all of the space. Let $c:\mathcal H\to\mathcal C$ be the cokernel of $f$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ and $x\in X$. Since $\mathcal H$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] there are an open $U\ni x$, a map $\alpha:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ with cokernel map $c_\alpha$ and an isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{Coker}\alpha\to\mathcal H|_U$; put $\pi=\theta\circ c_\alpha:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal H|_U$. Then $\pi$ is an epimorphism and $\pi\alpha=0$, and the complex $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal H|_U$ is exact at $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$: the image of $\alpha$ is the kernel of $c_\alpha$ by definition [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], and $\operatorname{Ker}\pi=\operatorname{Ker}c_\alpha$ since $\theta_W$ is injective on every open $W$ (kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). By step 1 (b) $c|_U$ is a cokernel of $f|_U$, and by step 1 (c) $\mathcal G|_U$ is of finite type. By step 1 (c) it suffices to show that $\mathcal C|_U$ is of finite presentation for each such $U$. Replacing $X$ by $U$ and $\mathcal G,\mathcal H,f,c$ by their restrictions, we may and do assume from now on that $U=X$: there is an exact sequence $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal H\to0$, $\mathcal G$ is of finite type, and $c:\mathcal H\to\mathcal C$ is a cokernel of $f$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0H96 (lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation), proof, lines 1440-1454: 'Locally on X, we can write F = O_X^n / M'

proof.text: The relations module $\mathcal M$ is of finite type. Let $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Ker}\pi\subseteq\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$, the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $W\mapsto\ker\pi_W$ with inclusion $j$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\alpha':\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal M$ the map with $j\alpha'=\alpha$ (it exists since $\pi\alpha=0$). As $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal H$ is exact at $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ (step 2), $\alpha'$ is an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift]. $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}$ is of finite type (step 1 (d)), so $\mathcal M$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-image-extension] (1).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0H96 (lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation), proof, lines 1440-1454: 'M ⊂ O_X^n is a finite type O_X-submodule'

proof.text: The image of $f$ is of finite type. Let $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Ker}c\subseteq\mathcal H$ (sectionwise, $\mathcal I(W)=\ker c_W$) with inclusion $i$; this is the image of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Since $cf=0$, $f=i\circ f'$ for a unique $f':\mathcal G\to\mathcal I$. The complex $\mathcal G\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal H\xrightarrow{c}\mathcal C$ is exact at $\mathcal H$ (step 1 (b)), so $f'$ is an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift]; as $\mathcal G$ is of finite type, $\mathcal I$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-image-extension] (1).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0H96 (lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation), proof, lines 1440-1454: 'The O_X-module Im(φ) is of finite type because G → Im(φ) is surjective and G is finite type'

proof.text: The preimage $\mathcal N$ of the image is of finite type. Let $\mathcal N=\operatorname{Ker}(c\pi)\subseteq\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$, sectionwise $\mathcal N(W)=\{t\in\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}(W):c_W(\pi_W(t))=0\}=\{t:\pi_W(t)\in\mathcal I(W)\}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\mathcal M(W)\subseteq\mathcal N(W)$ for all $W$, giving an inclusion $\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$, which is a monomorphism (injective on every $W$, so its sectionwise kernel is $0$), and $\pi$ restricts to $p:\mathcal N\to\mathcal I$, $p_W(t)=\pi_W(t)$, with $p\circ(\mathcal M\to\mathcal N)=0$. $p$ is an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1): for $s\in\mathcal I(W)\subseteq\mathcal H(W)$, $\pi$ being an epimorphism, the same lemma (1) gives an open covering $W=\bigcup_kW_k$ and $t_k\in\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}(W_k)$ with $\pi(t_k)=s|_{W_k}$; then $c\pi(t_k)=c(s)|_{W_k}=0$, so $t_k\in\mathcal N(W_k)$ and $p(t_k)=s|_{W_k}$. The complex $\mathcal M\to\mathcal N\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal I$ is exact at $\mathcal N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (2): if $t\in\mathcal N(W)$ and $p(t)=0$ then $\pi(t)=0$, i.e. $t\in\mathcal M(W)$ (trivial covering). Hence $0\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal N\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal I\to0$ is a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (this is $\operatorname{Im}(f)=\mathcal N/\mathcal M$ of the source). $\mathcal M$ (step 3) and $\mathcal I$ (step 4) are of finite type, so $\mathcal N$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-image-extension] (2).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0H96 (lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation), proof, lines 1440-1454: 'Im(φ) = N/M ... By Lemma 01B7, N is finite type' (Lemma 01B7, label lemma-extension-finite-type, line 855)

proof.text: $\mathcal C=\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}/\mathcal N$ is of finite presentation. Let $y\in X$. As $\mathcal N$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], there are an open $V\ni y$ and sections $t_1,\dots,t_s\in\mathcal N(V)$ whose map $\beta:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus s}\to\mathcal N|_V$ is an epimorphism. Let $k:\mathcal N\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ be the inclusion and $\gamma=k|_V\circ\beta:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus s}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}$ (the map of the sections $t_l$ viewed in $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}(V)$). The complex $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{\gamma}\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{(c\pi)|_V}\mathcal C|_V$ has composite $0$ (as $c\pi k=0$) and is exact at $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (2): for $W\subseteq V$ and $t\in\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}(W)$ with $c\pi(t)=0$ we have $t\in\mathcal N(W)$, and since $\beta$ is an epimorphism the same lemma (1) gives a covering $W=\bigcup_kW_k$ and $u_k\in\mathcal O_V^{\oplus s}(W_k)$ with $\beta(u_k)=t|_{W_k}$, i.e. $\gamma(u_k)=t|_{W_k}$. Moreover $c\pi$ is an epimorphism (a cokernel map composed with the epimorphism $\pi$), hence so is $(c\pi)|_V$ (step 1 (a)). By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (a), $(c\pi)|_V$ is a cokernel of $\gamma$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$, so $\mathcal C|_V$ is isomorphic to the cokernel of $\gamma:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus s}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}$ (two cokernels of the same morphism are isomorphic by their universal properties). As $y$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal C$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]; by step 2 this proves that $\operatorname{Coker}f$ is of finite presentation.

proof.text: The final clause: if $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal H$ are both of finite presentation, $\mathcal G$ is of finite type by step 1 (e) [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and steps 2-6 apply.
